# Fixed-facet meeting points without proper endpoint cuts

This note extends a finite-menu deformation certificate to full and
empty endpoint cuts, including supporting facets. It does not prove
the geometric loss threshold needed for OC. All bodies below are
full-dimensional in their continuous space; d>=1.

Let A,K,B be convex bodies at bases -1,0,1 with (A+B)/2 subset K.
Let y0 be in int K. Let v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole dependence
sum_i v_i=0. Put h_i=h_B(v_i). Suppose the actual through-source
caps with middle trace v_i.x>=v_i.y0 and B trace v_i.x>=h_i have
one common raw volume Q. Their A thresholds are

    b_i=2v_i.y0-h_i,
    U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=b_i}|.

The A cuts may be proper, full, or empty. K's cuts are all proper.
Choose any p in A and contract A_e=p+(1-e)(A-p), e>=0 small. This
is an actual compatible three-fiber family, since A_e subset A.

## 1. Scalar quantiles supply the meeting point

For each i define

    f_i(s,e)=|K intersect {v_i.x>=s}|
             +|A_e intersect {v_i.x>=2s-h_i}|.

Near s_i0=v_i.y0, K's proper section density is continuous and
bounded below by a positive constant. Consequently f_i is continuous
and strictly decreasing in s there, with a uniform strictly positive
lower bound on its decrease divided by an increase in s. This
remains true even at a supporting or exterior A threshold, because
the second term is nonincreasing.

Contraction changes A's indicator in L1 by exactly
a[1-(1-e)^d]=O(e), where a=|A|. Hence f_i(s,e) converges uniformly
to f_i(s,0), with error O(e). On a common small interval of q about Q,
there is therefore a unique local inverse s_i=t_i(q,e), continuous
in q,e and strictly decreasing in q. The inverses are uniformly
Lipschitz in changes of their function values by the preceding
lower slope bound. In particular t_i(Q,e)=s_i0+O(e).

At e=0, sum_i t_i(Q,0)=sum_i v_i.y0=0. The continuous function
q -> sum_i t_i(q,e) is strictly decreasing. At the two ends of a
sufficiently small fixed q interval its signs are opposite, by
continuity from e=0. It consequently has a unique zero q(e), and
the same lower-slope/inverse bounds show q(e)=Q+O(e). For clarity,
an upper bound on the s slopes is also available: convex-body
sections are uniformly bounded on a compact neighborhood, including
their one-sided endpoint limits. It gives a positive lower bound
on the absolute q slopes of the inverse functions and hence the
last O(e) claim. The vector (t_i(q(e),e)) has coordinate sum zero.
The linear map y -> (v_i.y)_i is an isomorphism onto this
d-dimensional sum-zero space. Thus it determines a unique

    y(e)=y0+O(e) in int K.

All displayed caps through this actual meeting point have raw
volume q(e). Their middle halfspaces cover R^d because their
normals sum to zero. Therefore EVERY middle-fiber point has raw
depth at most q(e), whether or not the menu remains critical.
Endpoint maxima remain their ordinary maxima, with A's multiplied
by (1-e)^d. This is an all-source upper certificate.

## 2. One-sided section densities at support planes

Write

    k_i=H_(d-1)(K intersect {v_i.x=s_i0})/||v_i||>0.

For the A cut define sigma_i as its normalized proper-section
measure when proper, its normalized supporting-face measure when
b_i=min_A v_i.x or b_i=max_A v_i.x, and zero when b_i is strictly
outside the support interval. Supporting faces of dimension less
than d-1 have sigma_i=0. In dimension1, a supporting face is a
singleton and its H_0 measure is1.

The interior section density approaches these face densities at
each support endpoint. To see this, identify nearby parallel planes
by translation. Compactness puts every limit point of the sections
in the supporting face. Conversely, interpolate every point of that
face toward one fixed interior point of A to approximate it on an
interior parallel plane. Compactness gives Hausdorff convergence;
convex (d-1)-volume converges, also to zero for a lower-dimensional
face. This proves the stated one-sided limits. For d=1 they are
immediate.

Set c_i=b_i-v_i.p. For a scalar source velocity z_i=v_i.y'(0),
the exact homothety formula shows that the A contribution has the
following first-order responses:

    proper:                -dU_i-sigma_i(2z_i+c_i),
    full at min support:   -da-sigma_i(2z_i+c_i)_+,
    empty at max support:   sigma_i(-2z_i-c_i)_+,
    strictly full:         -da,
    strictly empty:         0.                            (1)

These expansions are uniform for bounded z_i. This follows by
integrating the continuous proper density or its one-sided endpoint
limit over an interval of length O(e), and by the exact pulled-back
threshold

    [2(s_i0+e z_i)-h_i-e v_i.p]/(1-e)
       =b_i+e(2z_i+c_i)+O(e^2).

The positive-part formula retains a supporting face's first-order
mass instead of treating that zero-volume trace as irrelevant.

## 3. A unique directional derivative and its exact weights

Let R_i(z_i) be -k_i z_i plus the applicable response in (1).
It is continuous, strictly decreasing, piecewise affine, and its
every slope is at most -k_i<0. Thus R_i maps R onto R and has a
continuous strictly decreasing inverse. There is exactly one number
q_dot satisfying

    sum_i R_i^(-1)(q_dot)=0.                             (2)

Existence follows because the sum tends to opposite infinities at
the two ends of the real line. The meeting-point O(e) estimates
and the uniform expansions imply that every subsequential limit
of ((q(e)-Q)/e,(y(e)-y0)/e) solves (2) and its associated scalar
equations. Their uniqueness proves that the full right derivatives
exist. In particular the z_i are one simultaneous source velocity
with sum_i z_i=0, not separately optimized velocities.

There are coefficients theta_i in [0,1] giving the exact equivalent
form

    q_dot=-(k_i+2theta_i sigma_i)z_i
                -dU_i-theta_i sigma_i c_i.               (3)

For a proper cut theta_i=1. At minimum support it is1 when
2z_i+c_i>0 and0 when that expression is negative. At maximum
support it is1 when that expression is negative and0 when positive.
At a zero expression any value gives the same response; choose
any one. Strict exterior cuts have sigma_i=0 and may use theta_i=0.
These choices are dictated by the common solution; they are not
independently adjustable allocations in a claimed optimum.

Put

    w_i=1/(k_i+2theta_i sigma_i)>0, W=sum_i w_i.

Multiplying (3) by w_i and summing cancels the actual source motion,
and gives the exact formula

    q_dot=-sum_i w_i[dU_i+theta_i sigma_i(b_i-v_i.p)]/W.    (4)

This agrees with the proper-cut certificate when every theta_i=1.
Without the common solution of (2), choosing arbitrary theta_i in
(4) need not reproduce the actual derivative.

## 4. Sharp centroid payment remains valid for every active allocation

Choose the ONE actual point p=g_A. For a proper cap, the sharp
centroid-loss theorem applies to its summand in (4). For a full cap
strictly containing A the summand is da. For a full cap at minimum
support, every theta in [0,1] satisfies

    da+theta sigma_i(b_i-v_i.g_A)>=d^2 a/(d+1).           (5)

Indeed at that minimum level the cap-root has left derivative0 and
right derivative -sigma_i/[d a^((d-1)/d)]. Concavity makes every
intermediate slope a global upper supporting slope. If theta sigma_i
is positive, its associated cone comparison has lower support0,
total a, and mean at most da/[(d+1)theta sigma_i]. This is exactly
(5). If theta sigma_i=0, (5) follows from da>=d^2a/(d+1).
This is the same signed layer-cake proof as the proper-cap theorem,
with comparison fraction1, not an unproved boundary limit.

For an empty cap, b_i>=max_A v_i.x>v_i.g_A, so its summand in (4)
is nonnegative. Consequently, if

    psi_d(U)=U^((d-1)/d) for U>0, and psi_d(0)=0,

the exact weights determined above obey

    -q_dot >=[d^2/(d+1)] a^(1/d)
                         sum_i w_i psi_d(U_i)/W.          (6)

For d=1 this convention gives psi_1(U)=1 for positive U and0 at0;
there is no undefined 0^0. All full captures, empty captures and
supporting faces are retained. The weights still depend on the
actual one-sided source response, so no geometric balance condition
has been inferred from (6) alone.

## 5. Limits of the certificate

If Q is the original globally maximal depth and both endpoint
ordinary maxima have strict gaps below Q, the actual normalized
depth strictly decreases whenever -q_dot>d a Q/(a+|K|+|B|).
This follows by differentiating the upper certificate q(e) divided
by total mass, whose derivative is -da. The all-source menu and
endpoint gaps justify that comparison exactly as in the proper-cut
case. Tied endpoints require a separate multi-rate response analysis;
they are not resolved here. Nor does this note supply the numerical
loss condition or a general critical-menu classification.
